messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • INC-2026 • P1 • hosted-api v2 high 5xx rate detected. Auto-page applied: primary oncall. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p1-5xx :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Summary: spike started ~22:10 UTC, 10m sustained elevated 5xxs, frontend error ratio 18%. Impact: degraded response for ~15% of text-generation requests. Paging groups: eng-runtime -> eng-infra -> eng-security.

alex g: I'm primary oncall for the next 2h (until 00:10 UTC). Simon you're secondary?

simon: Yep I'm secondary. I'll start triage with runtime. Maria can you confirm if any recent model rollouts or config changes?

maria z: No rollout on hosted-api v2 in the last 6h. We did a maintenance job on the KV cache cluster earlier but that targeted embeddings pipeline only. Not sure it's related.

alex g: K, initial checks: 1) check NLB error logs 2) check runtime logs for OOMs/timeouts 3) validate latency/queue length. I'm running these now.

jamie: Also flagging support — customers in EU may see failures. @support-oncall please prepare customer-facing note if we confirm degraded service.

infra-oncall: Looking at NLB metrics — spike in 5xx at same time as backend connection errors to runtime pool-3. Something at the TCP layer: many resets. I'm opening an infra ticket.

maria z: Runtime logs show repeated KV cache misses with timeout retries to remote cache proxy. A few requests bubble up as 502 from runtime. Pasting error snippet:

```
2026-03-14T22:12:08Z runtime.main ERROR request_id=abc123 upstream=cache-proxy timeout after 1500ms
2026-03-14T22:12:09Z runtime.worker ERROR OOM while allocating 1.2GB model buffer
```

alex g: OOMs are concerning. Could be memory pressure from long-context requests. Any recent changes to max_seq_len or batching?

maria z: No config toggles. However the maintenance Jamie mentioned touched the cache cluster; maybe cache-proxy started returning errors causing runtime to rehydrate KV cache often -> memory spikes.

simon: If cache-proxy is flapping we should route traffic to a fallback model variant that doesn't use remote cache. We have a canary variant `hosted-api-v2-no-cache`.

alex g: Good idea. Who can flip routing? infra-oncall or I can apply a quick routing rule. Need to confirm risk of increased cost/latency.

infra-oncall: I can route ~30% of traffic to the no-cache variant via the routing control plane. Command:

```bash
# route 30% to fallback
rctl set-route hosted-api-v2 --split 70:hosted-api-v2,30:hosted-api-v2-no-cache
```
I'll do that in 2 mins after snapshotting metrics.

support-oncall: Preparing templated update. If we route 30% to no-cache should we mention increased latency but lower failures? I'll draft: "We are mitigating elevated 5xx errors by routing a portion of traffic to a fallback variant; some requests may see higher latency."

alex g: Perfect. Security: any risk with switching variants?

security-oncall: Not seeing any IAC changes risk here. Ensure the fallback variant uses same model weights and data policies. If it uses a different infra pool, confirm that private keys/KMS access remains scoped. I will review access logs while you flip.

oncall-bot: NOTE • Alerting: paging escalation to eng-infra and eng-runtime complete. Channel autopopulated with incident workspace.

infra-oncall: Route applied. Monitoring metrics now. 5xx rate on the main pool dropped from 18% -> 9% in the first 90s. No-cache variant latency +120ms p50 observed.

maria z: Runtime OOM count decreased after routing. Looks like cache-proxy timeouts were forcing huge rehydration and buffer growth.

alex g: Great. Action items: 1) Infra to continue investigating cache-proxy cluster (infra-oncall) 2) Runtime to add a temporary circuit-breaker on cache proxy calls (maria) 3) Support to prepare customer comms (support-oncall) 4) Security to audit access for fallback variant (security-oncall). Anyone want to own the incident doc? I'll own the incident tracker notes.

simon: I'll take the postmortem on runtime side. Will add suggested mitigation (short-term: circuit-breaker, longer-term: local cache warmers).

support-oncall: Draft posted to incident doc: "We have routed a portion of traffic to a fallback variant; we're monitoring. Estimated impact window 22:10-ongoing. We'll update every 30m or when we have a clear remediation."

security-oncall: I've started a scoped review. No immediate block. Will post findings to incident thread.

jamie: Heads-up: I start shift takeover at 00:10 UTC. Alex please ping me on Slack 10m before handoff with current status. If the routing remains >0% to fallback at handoff, we should keep coverage until cache-proxy is healthy.

alex g: Will do. Also note a coverage gap tomorrow 04:00-06:00 UTC where neither oncall-primary is scheduled (holiday overlap). Can we schedule a backup? @simon can you cover that 2h window or nominate someone?

simon: I can cover the 04:00-06:00 UTC slot. Adding to schedule.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF REMINDER • Alex G handing off to Jamie at 00:10 UTC. Please update the oncall calendar if anything changes.

infra-oncall: Root cause so far: cache-proxy nodes running GC/OOM cycles after maintenance job; network resets between proxy and runtime observed. We're rolling a stable cluster build and will cordon problematic nodes. ETA 40m.

maria z: I'll implement a temporary per-request circuit breaker: if cache-proxy timeout > 200ms, fall back to local in-memory small cache. Pushing patch to staging, will hotfix to prod after quick smoke.

alex g: Thanks. Please post the hotfix commands here.

maria z: Hotfix snippet:

```yaml
# runtime config override (temporary)
cache:
  remote_proxy_timeout_ms: 200
  local_fallback_enabled: true
```
Will apply via config flip: `cfg apply runtime/hosted-api-v2 --override cache.*`

infra-oncall: Cordon and redeploy started. Rolling one proxy node at a time to avoid blast radius.

support-oncall: Customer comms updated: added ETA and mitigations. Posting to status page now.

alex g: Good progress. Keep updates here. Jamie I'll ping you at 00:00 UTC for handoff. Current incident severity remains P1 until cache-proxy is stable and routing returns to 100% main pool.

jamie: Copy. I'll take over at 00:10. If infra hasn't stabilized by then I'll continue the page rotation and call for an on-call war room.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • INC-2026 • Routing applied -> 30% fallback -> 5xx rate trending down. Next auto-update in 30m.

simon: Adding runbook note: when remote cache starts timing out, immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic to no-cache variant 2) reduce remote_proxy_timeout 3) cordon proxy nodes 4) apply local_fallback. I'm editing https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p1-5xx to include that.

alex g: Thanks. Closing loop: once infra confirms proxy cluster healthy and 5xx < 1% for 30m we will lift routing split back to 100% main. Agree?

participants will update status as they have changes.

(End of thread for now)
